newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols falter before jobs report.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols falter before jobs report.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options softened Thursday on the eve of the May employment data as some market participants got an early jump on the expected post-report trend, traders said.
Bond volatility typically declines sharply immediately following the release of the number as traders remove risk premium from the options.

Traders said the volatility selling seen Thursday also underscored an expectation that futures would continue to trade in fairly narrow ranges after the jobs report, an indicator that has a history of sparking violent price swings.
"They are already hitting it before the number tomorrow in anticipation of us not moving," said an options broker for a U.S. banking firm.

July Treasury bond volatility ended at 8.95 percent, down from 9.10 percent on the opening but above the 8.70 percent quoted late Wednesday. September was 8.45 percent, down from 8.55 percent at the opening and 8.50 percent for the previous session.
September bond futures ended 1/32 lower at 110-00.
In bond options, traders said a New York dealer firm sold 3,000 July 109-00 puts covered against futures at 109-23.
In Eurodollars, several large put purchases were noted, with the December 93.50 strike popular, and a Wall Street firm bought a total of 9,000 of the December 94.00 calls.
Volatility values were unchanged at 9.0 percent for September options and 10.9 percent for December.
Selling of short-dated July and September straddles was a feature, though volatilities there also held steady, at 16.0 percent in July and 15.3 percent in September.
